blocks.text: Pan first taught to join several reeds with wax. — — — — —

Corpses were embalmed with wax no less than with honey. Thus Herodotus in book 4 reports that the Scythians carried the body of a dead king, κατακεκηρωμένον [katakekērōmenon], throughout all Scythia before burying it. And in book 1 the same author says of the Persians: κατακηρώσαντες τὸν νεκρὸν γῇ κρύπτουσι [katakērōsantes ton nekron gē kryptousi]. Hence Cicero, Tusculan Disputations book 1: the Persians embalm them after coating them with wax, so that the bodies may last as long as possible. And [col. 531] Strabo, book 15: Θάπτουσι δὲ κηρῷ περιπλάσσοντες τὰ σώματα [Thaptousi de kērō periplassontes ta sōmata]. So the well-known word موميا [mūmiyā] mumia seems to be derived from موم [mūm] mum. So the Persians call wax, and the Arabs call προπόλιν [propolin]. And the words of Isaiah, chapter 64, verse 2, כקדוח אש המסים מים, the Elders render thus: Ὡς κηρὸς ἀπὸ προσώπου πυρὸς τήκεται [Hōs kēros apo prosōpou pyros tēketai]. For in place of מים, that is, waters, they read מום, that is, wax; and כקדם אש, as before fire, in place of כקדוח אש, as fire burns. So already at that time the word מום mum was in use for wax, whence mumia. Wax was also much used in writing, in writing tablets, in painting, in cosmetics, and in seals, a use that lasts to this day. But these matters belong elsewhere.

The sacred writers often compare things with wax melting before fire. Thus David, Psalm. XXII, 15: My heart is like wax, it melts within me. And Psal. LXVIII, 3: As wax melts before fire, so the wicked perish before God. And Psal. XCVII, 5: The mountains melt like wax before the Lord. And Mich. I, 4: The mountains shall melt under him, and the valleys shall be cleft, like wax before the fire. Hence the writer of the book of Judith, whoever he is, chapter 16, verse 18: The rocks [III, 398] shall melt like wax at your presence. So too the profane authors everywhere. Theocritus in the Pharmaceutria:
Ὡς τοῦτον τὸν καρὸν ἐγὼ, σὺν δαίμονι, τάκω, [Hōs touton ton karon egō, syn daimoni, takō,] Ὡς τάκοιθ᾽ ὑπ᾽ ἔρωτος ὁ Μύνδιος αὐτίκα Δέλφις. [Hōs takoith᾽ hyp᾽ erōtos ho Myndios autika Delphis.]
As I, with the god's help, melt this wax, so may Delphis of Myndus at once melt with love. Hence Virgil:
As this clay hardens, and as this wax melts in one and the same fire, so may Daphnis with love of me.

Moreover, when the clouds too are thinned by the winds, or are dissolved when struck from above by the heat of the sun, they let fall rainy moisture, dripping, as when wax wasting over a hot fire melts abundantly.
He could bear it no longer, but as yellow wax wastes in a gentle fire, and morning frost in the sun, so, worn away by love, he melts and is slowly consumed by a hidden fire.
And in book 10, on the statue of Pygmalion:
It yielded under his fingers and gave way, as Hymettian wax softens in the sun. — — — —
Lucan on Sabellus, who had been bitten by the seps serpent, book 9, verse 783:
— — his shoulders melt, and his strong arms; his neck and head flow away; not faster does snow dissolve and fall before the warm South Wind, nor will wax yield to the sun.
Τήκομαι ὡς κηρὸς παρ᾽ πυρὶ, κάλλος ὁρῶν· [Tēkomai hōs kēros par᾽ pyri, kallos horōn;]
I melt like wax at the fire, beholding beauty.

Wax is called in Hebrew דונג, but in Chaldee שעוה; hence the Hebrew verb השתעה means to soften like wax, if we believe the masters, who render these words of Es. XLI, 10., אל תשתע כי אני אלהיך, roughly in this sense: Do not soften (like wax), for I am your God. So R. Selomo. And Kimchi observes that his forebears interpreted it thus, namely in Bereshit Rabba, section 65, in these words: כיון שאמר [III, 399] יצחק ליעקוב גשה נא ואמשוכך בני נשפכו מים על שוקיו והיה לבו רפה כשעוה וזמן לו הקדוש ברוך הוא שני מלאכים אחד בימינו ואחד בשמאלו והיו אוחזין אותו במרפקו כדי שלא יפול הדא הוא דכתיב אל תשתע כי אני אלהיך, When Isaac said to Jacob (who was hiding under Esau's garment to obtain the blessing), Genes. XXVII, 21. „Come near, I pray, my son, that I may touch you“: his legs ran with sweat, [col. 532] and his heart softened like wax. But God, holy and blessed, prepared for him two angels, one on his right, the other on his left, to hold him under the arm so that he would not fall. Hence what is said in Es. XLI, 10. „Do not soften (like wax), for I am your God.“
